today_summary: GCM26 prints $4,107.8 on the 10-15 snapshot, -$69.4 (-1.66%) and a clean break of the five-day box floor at $4,156.9 — the largest one-day move of the cycle and 1.39x the $49.99 1-sigma envelope. ATM IV did not bid: it held exactly 19.32% through a 1.66% down day, so the break was absorbed with no vol premium and no cushion. Local net GEX inside ±$200 deteriorated to -271.4 (calls +191.4 against puts -462.8), the most short-gamma reading of the window, while the gamma flip migrated up to $4,900 and left spot $792 below it. Participation finally came home — 16.1% of a 15,432-contract tape traded within ±$200 of spot, a five-day high versus 9.0% yesterday, with put volume +87% to 3,449.
five_day_thesis: Five sessions have netted -$49.1 (-1.18%), $4,156.9 to $4,107.8, but the shape of the tape inverted in the last 24 hours: four sessions of $4,156.9-$4,216.2 chop ended in a 1.66% break, and the $4,187 shelf that framed the whole week is now $79 overhead. The dealer cushion, not the price, is what deteriorated: total chain GEX has collapsed from 432.0 on 10-12 to 179.6 (-58.4%), the ±20% window metric from 210.02 to 26.26, and local ±$200 net GEX from -113.5 at Monday's best to -271.4 — the gamma flip walked $4,750 to $4,900 (+$150), so dealers are shorter gamma at the money than at any point in the window with price further from the stabilizing zone. Flow composition reversed just as sharply: calls fell from 89.6% to 77.7% of volume, far-OTM call share (strikes ≥$6,000) from 42.3% to 15.2%, and ATM participation doubled 9.0% to 16.1% — the tail-convexity lottery of midweek was replaced by real near-the-money hedging. The defensive build that had been quietly accumulating all week confirmed on the break: put OI added +496 at $3,950, +466 at $3,700 and +328 at $3,750 over five days, and 864 lots traded the $3,750 strike alone yesterday, 8.7% below spot. What has not moved is the pinning structure — P/C OI is frozen at 0.39 for all five sessions, the $3,500 put wall and $5,500 call wall have not migrated once, and global max pain sits $1,392 (33.9%) overhead with no interior minimum; the only pain level with any local meaning drifted down to $4,325 from $4,350.
what_changed: Spot $4,107.8, -$69.4 (-1.66%) — a 1.39-sigma move and the first close outside the five-day $4,156.9-$4,216.2 box, confirming yesterday's sub-$4,140 bearish trigger
ATM IV unchanged at 19.32% through a 1.66% down day — vol refused to bid the break, holding 1-sigma at $49.99 (1.22%)
Local net GEX -271.4 from -199.5, a five-day extreme, with put gamma -462.8 now 2.4x call gamma +191.4
Gamma flip migrated $4,800 → $4,900 while spot fell $69 — the short-gamma gap widened to $792 from $618
ATM participation 16.1% of a 15,432-contract tape, a five-day high and double yesterday's 9.0%; far-OTM call share collapsed 42.3% → 15.2%
Put OI built +468 at $3,950, +304 at $3,750, +277 at $4,000 and +245 at $4,100 in one session — a continuous defensive ladder from the money down to -9.9%
prediction: Bias bearish while $4,150 caps, with the 1-sigma envelope $4,057.8-$4,157.8 now sitting entirely below the broken box — a short-gamma market that has just lost a four-session floor on rising near-the-money participation continues rather than reverts, and unchanged 19.32% IV means the move is not yet crowded. Downside path runs $4,100 (2,445 put OI) to $4,050 (2,520 OI) and then the $4,000 wall (4,596 OI, net GEX -54.93, the most negative near-field strike), with $3,950 (3,078 OI) and $3,900 (4,229 OI) behind it. The bear case invalidates on a reclaim of $4,150, and above $4,175 — the first strike where net GEX turns positive at +7.89 — the tape re-opens $4,200 (1,710 call OI) and the $4,300 shelf (2,167 call OI); $5,500 max pain exerts no pull from 33.9% overhead at 41 DTE.
